_readme: Competitions are competitive events with rules, eligibility, judging, and prizes.
They are distinct from general events (workshops, talks, etc.).
short_description       one or two lines for cards
venue                   location string or '' when not confirmed
min_team_size           minimum team size (1 for individual)
prizes                  object with first, second, third, participation
is_published            boolean, visible on public site

competitions.title: Dance Battle
competitions.short_description: Solo and group dance competition across multiple styles — hip-hop, contemporary, classical and fusion.
competitions.description: Dance Battle is the flagship performing arts competition of Cultura. Dancers compete in solo and group categories across multiple styles including hip-hop, contemporary, classical Indian, and fusion. The competition runs in two rounds: a preliminary showcase and a final battle round where finalists perform head-to-head. Judging criteria include technique, creativity, stage presence, musicality, and overall impact. Open to all students regardless of dance background.
competitions.eligibility: Open to all students of the participating institution. No prior dance experience required.
rules: Participants may enter solo or as a group (2-8 members).
Music must be submitted in advance in MP3 format.
Props are allowed but must be approved by the organizers 24 hours before the event.
Costumes should be appropriate for a college cultural festival.
Each performance has a strict time limit: 3 minutes for solo, 5 minutes for groups.
Judging decisions are final and binding.

faq.question: Can I participate in both solo and group categories?
faq.answer: Yes, you can enter both categories but you must register separately for each.

faq.question: What dance styles are allowed?
faq.answer: All styles are welcome — hip-hop, contemporary, classical, folk, fusion, Bollywood, etc.

competitions.title: Music Showdown
competitions.short_description: Battle of the bands and solo musicians — original compositions and covers welcome.
competitions.description: Music Showdown brings together the best student musicians for a battle of talent. Bands and solo artists compete in separate categories. Performances can be original compositions or creative covers. The competition features a live audience and a panel of music industry professionals as judges. Winners get studio recording time and performance slots at the main festival stage.
competitions.eligibility: Open to all students. Bands must have 2-6 members, all from the same institution.
rules: Bands: 2-6 members. Solo: 1 performer (may use backing tracks).
At least one original composition is required for bands category.
Sound check will be scheduled 2 hours before the event.
Drum kit, amps, and basic PA will be provided. Bring your own instruments.
Performance time: 15 minutes for bands, 10 minutes for solo.
No profanity or offensive content in lyrics.

prizes.first: Studio recording session (8 hours) + Main stage slot

faq.question: Can I use a backing track for solo performance?
faq.answer: Yes, solo performers may use high-quality backing tracks on a USB drive.

faq.question: Is there a piano/keyboard provided?
faq.answer: Yes, a digital piano will be available on stage.

competitions.title: Fashion Parade
competitions.short_description: Student designers showcase original collections on the runway — themes announced on the spot.
competitions.description: Fashion Parade is Cultura's premier fashion design competition. Student designers create and present original collections based on a theme announced 48 hours before the event. Collections are judged on creativity, wearability, craftsmanship, and thematic interpretation. Models can be fellow students or professional. The winning collection gets featured in the festival's official lookbook and a mentorship opportunity with a fashion industry partner.
competitions.eligibility: Open to all students. Design background not required but garment construction skills are essential.
rules: Teams of 1-3 designers. Each team presents a mini-collection of 3-5 looks.
Theme announced 48 hours before the competition.
Garments must be original designs created by the team.
Teams must provide their own models (can be fellow students).
Runway time: 3 minutes per team.
Judging includes a brief designer statement (1 minute).

prizes.first: Mentorship with fashion designer + Lookbook feature

faq.question: Do I need to be a fashion design student?
faq.answer: No, any student with garment-making skills can participate.

faq.question: Can I use recycled/upcycled materials?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Sustainable fashion is encouraged and may score bonus points.

competitions.title: Photography Contest
competitions.short_description: Capture the spirit of campus life — themed photo competition with exhibition.
competitions.description: The Photography Contest challenges students to capture compelling images around a given theme. Submissions are displayed in a physical exhibition during the festival and judged by professional photographers. Categories include: Campus Life, Portraits, Abstract/Creative, and Documentary. Winners receive camera gear and have their work featured in the festival's official gallery.
competitions.eligibility: Open to all students. Any camera type allowed (phone, DSLR, mirrorless, film).
rules: Individual entry only. Maximum 3 photos per participant.
Theme: 'Moments that Define Us' — interpret freely.
Photos must be taken during the current academic year.
Basic editing allowed (exposure, contrast, color). No heavy manipulation or AI generation.
Submit high-resolution files (min 3000px on longest edge).
Include a brief artist statement (max 100 words) per photo.

faq.question: Can I submit photos taken on my phone?
faq.answer: Yes! Phone photography is welcome and has its own merit category.

faq.question: Is there a printing fee?
faq.answer: No, the festival covers printing costs for the exhibition.

competitions.title: Literary Slam
competitions.short_description: Poetry slam, storytelling, and creative writing — perform your words live.
competitions.description: Literary Slam is Cultura's celebration of the spoken and written word. The competition has three categories: Poetry Slam (performance poetry), Storytelling (original short stories told live), and Creative Writing (submitted pieces judged on the page). Participants can enter multiple categories. The slam rounds are high-energy with audience participation, while the writing category allows for more reflective pieces.
competitions.eligibility: Open to all students. No prior publication or performance experience required.
rules: Categories: Poetry Slam (performed), Storytelling (performed), Creative Writing (submitted).
Poetry/Storytelling: 3-minute time limit per piece. Original work only.
Creative Writing: Submit up to 2 pieces (poetry max 40 lines, prose max 2000 words).
No hate speech, explicit content, or plagiarism.
Slam rounds: 2 rounds, top scorers advance to finals.
Writing submissions due 1 week before the event.

faq.question: Can I enter multiple categories?
faq.answer: Yes, you can enter Poetry Slam, Storytelling, and Creative Writing simultaneously.

faq.question: Do I need to memorize my poem for the slam?
faq.answer: Memorization is encouraged but not required. You may use a small note card.

competitions.title: Coding Marathon
competitions.short_description: 24-hour hackathon — build innovative solutions to real-world problems.
competitions.description: The Coding Marathon is a 24-hour hackathon where teams build software solutions to challenge statements revealed at the start. Open to all skill levels — beginners welcome! Mentors from the tech industry will be available throughout. Projects are judged on innovation, technical complexity, design, and potential impact. Prizes include cash, internships, and tech swag.
competitions.eligibility: Open to all students. Teams of 2-4. At least one member should have basic coding skills.
rules: Teams of 2-4 members. Cross-institution teams allowed.
Challenge statements revealed at kickoff.
All code must be written during the 24-hour period.
Open-source libraries and APIs allowed. No pre-written project code.
Final presentation: 5-minute demo + 3-minute Q&A.
Projects must be deployed and accessible via URL for judging.

faq.question: Can beginners participate?
faq.answer: Yes! We welcome all skill levels. Mentors will be available to help.

faq.question: What tech stack can I use?
faq.answer: Any language/framework. Web, mobile, AI, blockchain — anything goes.
